**Why binary search needs sorted data**

Binary search works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. It starts at the middle element of the array and decides whether to continue searching the left half or the right half based on a comparison with the target value. This decision relies on the fact that *all elements to the left of the current position are ≤ the current element* and *all elements to the right are ≥ the current element*. That ordering property can only be guaranteed if the whole array is sorted.
